📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that DIRECTOR PETER BERG had never made a World War II movie before The Mosquito Bowl, but he certainly knows a thing or two about football.
  • Berg’s new Netflix film dramatizes the stories of football players John McLaughry (Nicholas Galitzine), Tony Butkovich (Ray Nicholson), Bob Bauman (Bill Skarsgård), and Dave Schreiner (Tom Francis), who traded the NFL draft for military service.
  • The Mosquito Bowl underlines the devastating impact WWII’s casualty count had on an entire generation of young athletes, and the film unites its twin focuses of war and football by their mutual sense of brotherhood.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that DIRECTOR PETER BERG had never made a World War II movie before The Mosquito Bowl, but he certainly knows a thing or two about football. The director of Friday Night Lights has returned to a world of cocksure young players with their whole lives ahead of them in dire need of rousing their morale—only now it’s the true story of the football game between two World War II Marine regiments at Guadalcanal on Christmas Eve 1944. There’s another connection: both The Mosquito Bowl and Friday Night Lights are adapted from books by author Buzz Bissinger.

Berg’s new Netflix film dramatizes the stories of football players John McLaughry (Nicholas Galitzine), Tony Butkovich (Ray Nicholson), Bob Bauman (Bill Skarsgård), and Dave Schreiner (Tom Francis), who traded the NFL draft for military service. After enduring years of the Pacific campaign, they realize how valuable the team spirit and camaraderie of football can be as the Battle of Okinawa looms ahead of them.

The Mosquito Bowl underlines the devastating impact WWII’s casualty count had on an entire generation of young athletes, and the film unites its twin focuses of war and football by their mutual sense of brotherhood. The deeply felt connection between soldiers is the lifeblood of historical war films; when done convincingly, a squad’s well-earned devotion and loyalty add rich melodrama to the action. Brotherhood is just as compelling when it is subverted—like the respect felt between soldiers on opposing sides, or when hardened, broken combatants struggle to express the empathy and compassion they feel. The best war movies know that brotherhood endures after the fighting stops, but in different forms—softer, stranger, when it’s hard to reconcile the memories of war with a world that continues as normal.

To mark the Thanksgiving release of The Mosquito Bowl on Netflix, we ranked the most gripping and rousing war films about brotherhood.

An ensemble of actors you'd typically see in a "Young Stars of Tomorrow" profile immerse themselves in a U.S. Navy SEAL platoon and recreate a real-time Iraq War firefight that co-director Ray Mendoza was a part of. Opening with the platoon jubilantly dancing to "Call On Me" streamed through their base's crappy internet, Warfare promptly adopts a stripped-back and meticulous play-by-play of how one slice of warfare was actually experienced. You get a sense of brotherhood from the practiced, reflexive interactions between SEALs, and their interdependence also helped build the film, as Mendoza and co-director Alex Garland drew from the testimonies of his fellow soldiers when writing the script. The stylistic choices—like a thundering sound mix and infrequent use of satellite photography—add an extra layer of tension to Warfare's depiction of courage under fire. It’s one of the most visceral movies in recent memory about modern war.

Recent findings suggest that before he brought us high-octane visions of robot cops and ambitious showgirls, Paul Verhoeven directed a handful of smash hits in his native Netherlands, including this Golden Globe-nominated war epic about the diverging fates of Dutch students during the Nazi occupation. Led by a supremely dashing Rutger Hauer, Soldier of Orange begins in 1938 and follows the wartime trajectory of Erik Lanshof, an initially neutral but increasingly principled aristocrat who protects his Dutch Resistance friends and distances himself from fascist collaborators. Before long, his entire school group has pledged one type of loyalty or another. Observed over a period of time, war reveals everything, and Erik’s blossoming heroism emerges as a result of his friendships all changing—for better or worse.

Sources indicate that forgive us for taking a creative approach to the headline so early in the list: Hell in the Pacific features no battles or squadron camaraderie, and takes place on a deserted island with only two characters—an American pilot (Lee Marvin) and a Japanese army captain (Toshiro Mifune)—who don’t understand a word the other person claims. Even without comprehension, the American and Japanese soldiers find a hundred ways to rile each other up, including shock tactics, sabotage, pranks, and even makeshift imprisonment. Gradually, they realize each other’s company is the strongest connection to their starving humanity available to them, even if they’re affected in a way they can’t explain. Free from the rhetoric and politics of war, Marvin and Mifune play men who slip into a state of brash, stubborn childishness, and a brotherly kinship forms in spite of their inherent opposition.

In a recent development, clint Eastwood and Steven Spielberg sound like an odd pair to collaborate on a war picture, but Eastwood’s pared-down, melancholic visual style is a terrific fit for this post-Band of Brothers war movie. Flags of Our Fathers wasn’t received as positively as its Japanese-language companion film Letters from Iwo Jima, but it’s a robust and affecting watch—splitting its runtime between the overwhelming Battle of Iwo Jima and its aftermath, where three soldiers celebrated as the iconic “flag-raisers” spent the final year of the Pacific Campaign on a spiritually draining propaganda tour. Flags of Our Fathers takes the essential themes of war cinema—brotherhood, sacrifice, heroism—and juxtaposes them with the United States military manufacturing their own national images and narratives in real time. The tension between the brutal experience of being a brother-in-arms and the sanitized version promoted by war’s survivors makes for a powerful watch.

In a recent development, it’s as if director David Ayer (Suicide Squad, Bright) made a WWII movie to hammer home two points: tank warfare was a nightmare, and soldier hazing was way more hardcore than what you see in Band of Brothers. In the final months of the war in Europe, Wardaddy (Brad Pitt) rolls his bloody and battered tank unit slowly toward Berlin, and the arrival of fresh-faced pencil-pusher Norman (Logan Lerman) gives the hardened squad a chance to berate and bully the newcomer about all the ways he is soft, and war is hell. As their fellow brothers-in-arms are increasingly blasted apart into viscera, Wardaddy’s take-no-shit squad bolsters their unsentimental unity, and each of the five traumatized brothers rely on each other to watch their back and keep them sane on a frontline that might as well be the border to hell.

In a recent development, spike Lee’s bracing film about the scars of Vietnam takes a familiar concept—a jaded band of veterans who try to pull off a heist—and spins it in a thorny, unpredictable direction. Four older Black veterans (led by an intense, captivating, and Oscar-snubbed Delroy Lindo) return to ‘Nam to recover the CIA gold their squadron hid during the war—aside from a delayed payday, it’s also the ultimate memorial of their late squad leader Norman (Chadwick Boseman). Marked by years of bitterness and PTSD, the “Bloods” retrace their steps while juggling painful reflections on how the war left them angry and guilty. When they're ambushed in the jungle and have to pick up guns again, we're reminded that Lee is never satisfied sticking in one narrative mode for too long, but the jagged catharsis of cranky, once-loyal soldiers confronting their wounds is far more visceral to watch.

When Private Alex (Harry Styles) indicates, “We're regimental brothers, mate,” in the belly of a fishing trawler on Dunkirk Beach, he’s not acting nobly—he’s making the case for throwing a soldier he thinks is German (he’s actually French) to the Nazis surrounding them. So much of Christopher Nolan’s war film about the perilous evacuation of Allied troops from France’s northernmost beaches centers on division: soldier feuds, breakdowns in communication, and a nonlinear narrative that takes place over a week or an hour depending on who’s in front of the camera. But Dunkirk’s staggering disaster and survival action builds to an overwhelming climactic sense of unity. Across every mini-arc and timeline, Nolan demonstrates us countless pairs of soldiers, pilots, and civilians who stand together as symbolic brothers.

Sources indicate that after the famously gnarly and disorienting D-Day beach landing sequence—which has influenced every WWII action movie since, including The Mosquito Bowl—Saving Private Ryan settles into the most iconic band of brothers story outside of… well, Band of Brothers, co-created by this film’s director and star. Tom Hanks is the grouchy uncle leading a reluctant squad to rescue Private James Francis Ryan (Matt Damon) from the front lines after his brothers were killed in action. The squadron's trudge through France is fueled with banter, grumbling, and the type of resentment that stews between siblings who hate when someone receives special treatment. Steven Spielberg’s gift for balancing movie-star gravitas and off-the-cuff charisma is on full display in the ensemble, but no gruff, hot-tempered soldier has a response to Private Ryan's justification for not returning to his mom: “Tell her that when you found me, I was here, and I was with the only brothers I have left.”.

Industry observers note that the only war film on this list to be set before the 20th century and at sea, the Napoleonic Wars-era Master and Commander has a reputation for being a “dudes/gentlemen rock” classic: the reputation still holds up. Under the command of Captain Jack Aubrey (Russell Crowe), the HMS Surprise wages war against a French frigate that taunts the crew across the seas. Majestic naval battles aside, much of Master and Commander has a warm hangout tone, focusing on the kinship between Aubrey and ship’s surgeon Maturin, their interest in classical music and botanical science, and revelrous suppers in the captain’s quarters. It's impossible to watch Peter Weir’s sea epic and not pine for the brotherly loyalty (maybe not the seasickness or cannonball attacks) that Aubrey inspires here. Nothing will make you feel the romantic thrill of adventure like Master and Commander.

Industry observers note that pick your favorite scene from The Deer Hunter: the riotous wedding party, the spontaneous Frankie Valli singalong over a game of pool, or the exacting game of Russian roulette played by prisoners of war. They each shine a light on the ordinary, working-class brotherhood that was completely transformed by the Vietnam War. This Oscar-winning epic builds complex, traumatized characters (played by Robert De Niro, John Cazale, and Christopher Walken) who reckon with never being able to experience their relationships and community in the same way again. The Deer Hunter paints such a disturbing and fragile picture of the “before and after” of Vietnam, as each brotherly bond becomes charged with alienation and despair. Notorious for its multiple “death game” sequences, The Deer Hunter excels in making its harrowing portrayal of war and PTSD genuinely heartbreaking.

One of the best things to come out of legendary Hong Kong filmmakers John Woo and Tsui Hark falling out was the future director of Hard Boiled and Face/Off leaving the iconic A Better Tomorrow series to make this searing war story. Beginning in the late ’60s, it focuses on three close friends (Tony Leung, Jacky Cheung, Waise Lee) whose smuggling ambitions dunk them headfirst in the brutality and desperation of the Vietnam War. Bullet in the Head blends the epic sweep of New Hollywood war epics (Apocalypse Now, The Deer Hunter) with Woo’s “heroic bloodshed” toolkit, which meant electric action spectacle and bold, tragic melodrama. An underrated operatic beast in Woo’s stacked filmography—not to mention a personal one, as Woo used the film to express his reaction to the 1989 Tiananmen Square massacre—the action is always in service of a high-stakes tri-friendship that can only take so much passion and betrayal before the treasured brotherhood breaks.

According to recent reports, rory Doherty is a critic and journalist based in Edinburgh, Scotland. His work can be found at British GQ, Vulture, Inverse, AV Club, and other publications. He can be found on Twitter/X at @roryhasopinions.

Public EV charging is getting easier and faster, with more DC fast-charging ports available and services like Plug & Charge that streamline payment.

Eligible GM electric vehicle drivers enrolled in Energy Pass can now use the service at compatible Electrify America chargers.

The charge session is then billed through your preferred payment method with Energy Pass. You can view session details and receipts in the myChevrolet, myGMC, or myCadillac app.

During the rollout, GM stated drivers will still be able to use Charge by App and other charging methods.

First, you’ll need to enroll in GM’s Energy Pass in the myChevrolet, myGMC, or myCadillac app.

We just took a 10000 mile circuit of the US and part of Canada. Range anxiety is not really a thing. What was a thing was credit card anxiety, as in will it work. We had numerous failures, or multiple tries. Plug and charge is wonderful.

The new capabilities come after GM integrated the Electrify Network into the myChevrolet, myGMC, and myCadillac apps in January, adding more than 6,200 fast-charger options, most of which can deliver 350 kW.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

They may be small, but bear cubs have a pretty steep learning curve. In Alaska, brown bear (Ursus americanus) cubs have a roughly 50 percent survival rate within their first year, while the black bear (Ursus americanus) cub survival rate can range from 51 to 88 percent, depending on where they live. Cubs must learn how to fish, forage, find shelter, and climb trees to escape predators. Fortunately, biology helps out a bit with climbing. Bears have claws that curve and help them go up the tree and then back down safely.

One baby black bear who spent time at Anan Creek in southeastern Alaska’s Tongass National Forest highlighted off those climbing chops in style. The park’s rangers have officially awarded this bear with the 2026 Cutest Climber Award.

Industry observers note that “This little cub slipped on his way down but caught himself and hustled right after mom,” the rangers write. “An adorable reminder that even when you lose your footing, you can recover and keep going. A tiny, furry lesson in resilience provided by the bears of Anan.”.

Tongass National Forest’s rangers  are currently awarding the Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

Tongass is the largest national forest in the United States, and covers most of southeastern Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area includes Mendanhall Glacier (a popular destination for tourists on Alaskan cruises), numerous hiking trails, eagles soaring above, and plenty of bears on the hunt for food. One of the hotspots is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in Southeast Alaska. As such, the creek is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

In a recent development, according to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears and eight brown bears. Similar to  their chunky counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to feast on salmon and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear here has their own habits and quirks.

Recent findings suggest that the U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their antics.

Drug-Resistant ‘Superbugs’ Linked to More Than 50,000 Deaths a Year, CDC Says

📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (910 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fresh data show a substantial nationwide increase in potentially deadly infections caused by drug-resistant pathogens.
  • Sources indicate that the updated Antimicrobial Resistance (AR) Threats Report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) states that drug-resistant bacteria and fungi cause approximately 9.7 million infections in the United States each year.
  • The estimated deaths in the United States from these drug-resistant pathogens have also risen from 35,000 to 50,800.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fresh data show a substantial nationwide increase in potentially deadly infections caused by drug-resistant pathogens.

Sources indicate that the updated Antimicrobial Resistance (AR) Threats Report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) states that drug-resistant bacteria and fungi cause approximately 9.7 million infections in the United States each year. This is up from 2.8 million in a similar report from 2019.

The estimated deaths in the United States from these drug-resistant pathogens have also risen from 35,000 to 50,800.

It has been revealed that the newly introduced report also noted that infections that commonly occur in people in the hospital account for more than 42,000 deaths and cost the U.S. healthcare system more than $12 billion.

These findings are based on 2023 data. Officials from the CDC mentioned that the increase in drug-resistant infections from 2019 partially reflects a real rise in infections caused by certain resistant bacteria and fungi. However, they also noted that data sources and methodologies have changed, and direct comparisons between the two reports shouldn’t be made.

“These numbers are alarming by any measure but are particularly sobering when infectious diseases physicians connect real patients with these statistics in their everyday experience,” Wendy Armstrong, MD, President of the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA), remarked in a statement.

Industry observers note that the CDC report highlighted 19 drug-resistant pathogens responsible for the 9.7 million annual infections. Four of these pathogens are classified as urgent threats, 13 as serious threats, and 2 as concerning.

The CDC also maintains a watch list that currently includes six pathogens.

The four pathogens classified as urgent threats are:.

William Schaffner, MD, a professor of the Division of Infectious Diseases at Vanderbilt University Medical Center, told Healthline that the reason for this increase in superbugs is, “Overuse of antibiotics; using them for too long or in circumstances where they do not offer a benefit.”.

Sources indicate that “An example of the latter is the antibiotic treatment of common viral respiratory infections — antibiotics have no effect on viral infections. The widespread use of antibiotics kills off those bacteria that are susceptible to antibiotics, but then can leave a few bacterial survivors that are resistant to the effect of the antibiotics, resulting in the spread of these resistant strains,” he said.

Monica Gandhi, MD, a professor of medicine at the University of California, San Francisco, agreed and added, “This widespread use leads to selective drug pressure on the pathogen to evolve resistance to these antibiotics, making them harder to treat.”.

According to recent reports, “The risk to public health from these bugs is substantial. In fact, the World Health Organization (WHO) estimates up to 5 million deaths from these bugs worldwide every year, making these a substantial public health threat,” noted Gandhi.

Candida auris tops the list of urgent threats.

Industry observers note that cases have increased nearly tenfold since the first detection in hospitals 10 years ago. This includes a more than 50% jump between 2022 and 2023.

Sources indicate that candida auris is a fungus that is almost completely resistant to one class of antifungal medications. It has also shown emerging resistance to the other two classes.

This fungus is often found on people’s skin, spreads rapidly in healthcare settings like hospitals, and affects some of the most vulnerable individuals.

CRE is a family of multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens. They have become increasingly difficult to treat and can share resistance with other bacteria.

These bacteria also pose a significant threat to people in hospitals, especially those with devices such as ventilators and catheters. A recent study found that CRE cases at U.S. hospitals increased by 18% between 2019 and 2023.

While those in hospitals are especially vulnerable to CRE, 67% of the cases in 2023 were in the community. However, some of these cases may have occurred in people with recent exposure to healthcare.

Neisseria gonorrhoeae is the bacterium that causes gonorrhea, which is one of the most common sexually transmitted infections.

The CDC report noted that only a few antibiotics can effectively treat this infection.

Without effective treatment, gonorrhea can lead to:.

There are ways you can help prevent these superbugs:.

“[One] way individuals can help prevent the evolution of these superbugs is to not ask for antibiotics from their providers or urgent care settings in the setting of a viral infection,” said Gandhi.

Experts and organizations like the CDC are working together to find ways to reduce the spread of these superbugs.

“Professional organizations and hospitals are educating their doctors and staff about the antibiotic resistance problem and have created reviews of practice patterns to encourage the appropriate use of antibiotics,” said Schaffner.

Gandhi added that organizations should institute procedures, such as “antimicrobial stewardship programs,” to ensure that providers do not prescribe antibiotics for non-bacterial infections and narrow antibiotics as soon as possible.

The Pioneering Antimicrobial Subscriptions to End Upsurging Resistance (PASTEUR) Act aims to revitalize antibiotic and antifungal development by changing the way the federal government pays for novel antimicrobials.

This act was reintroduced in Congress in February and is at the moment under review.

The focus on reducing the spread of superbugs and developing new antibiotics is important.

“You really cannot have all the benefits of modern medicine, even outside the realm of infectious diseases, without effective antibiotics. It all goes away,” Haley Ann Pritchard, MD, medical director of infection prevention and antimicrobial stewardship at Eskenazi Health Hospital, said in a statement.

#121502. Tesla unveils 7.4 MW Powercore to take on ex-exec Baglino’s Heron Link

Tesla unveils 7.4 MW Powercore to take on ex-exec Baglino’s Heron Link

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1377 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, tesla has unveiled Powercore, a solid-state medium-voltage transformer that also handles the inverter and breaker functions in a single unit.
  • It’s made in America and scheduled to start operating in 2027.
  • Update: Tesla has since released a full spec sheet for Powercore, including efficiency, warranty, and its data center intends.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, tesla has unveiled Powercore, a solid-state medium-voltage transformer that also handles the inverter and breaker functions in a single unit. Tesla rates it at 7.4 MW (9 MVA) continuously at 34.5 kV, with grid-forming support up to 10 MVA of peak power.

It’s made in America and scheduled to start operating in 2027. That’s the same year Heron Power, the startup founded by Tesla’s former top engineer Drew Baglino, prepares to start volume production of its own solid-state transformer, the Heron Link.

Update: Tesla has since released a full spec sheet for Powercore, including efficiency, warranty, and its data center intends. We’ve updated the article with the upcoming details.

Recent findings suggest that tesla first noted it would build its own transformers in September 2025, when it unveiled Megapack 3 and Megablock. Megablock connects four Megapack 3 units to a transformer and switchgear, but Tesla shared next to nothing about the transformer itself.

Powercore is that missing piece. Tesla declared it today through its Tesla Megapack account on X:.

In a recent development, introducing PowercoreSolid state medium voltage transformer, inverter and breaker – reliable, safe and secure7.4 MW/9 MVA continuously at 34.5 kVac w/ grid-forming support for 10MVA of peak powerMade in America. Operating 2027 pic.twitter.com/sHxqnpWJrf.

About an hour later, Tesla followed up with a much longer post on X laying out the full spec sheet:.

It also packs a built-in solid-state medium-voltage breaker that Tesla states clears faults up to 1,000x faster than a conventional breaker. There’s no flammable oil, and it’s modular, so components can be serviced in the field without swapping the whole unit.

Tesla is pitching one product for three markets: battery storage, utility-scale solar, and 800 Vdc data centers. For Megablock, Powercore replaces the current two-step setup, where Megapack’s inverters output 480 V AC before a separate transformer steps it up to medium voltage. Tesla indicates that old architecture had twice the losses. For solar, Powercore works as a central inverter for today’s 1,500 Vdc arrays and upcoming 2,000 Vdc systems.

In a recent development, tesla still hasn’t shared pricing, customers, or a factory location. It only notes Powercore will be made in the US “of U.S. and imported parts” with first units operating in 2027.

In a recent development, the idea behind a solid-state transformer is simple enough. A typical solar or battery project uses low-voltage inverters to convert DC into AC, then a massive oil-filled, iron-core transformer to step that up to grid voltage. A solid-state unit does both jobs with silicon carbide power electronics, which means less gear, a smaller footprint, and active control over voltage and frequency. That control is what “grid-forming” means: the unit can help hold the grid steady instead of just following it.

And with lead times on conventional transformers stretching into years as data centers and renewable projects pile into interconnection queues, there’s real demand for an alternative.

You can’t look at Powercore without thinking of Heron Power.

Sources indicate that baglino spent 18 years at Tesla and finished as SVP of powertrain and energy, in charge of batteries, motors, power electronics, and energy products. He left in April 2024 and rolled out Heron Power in 2025 to build solid-state transformers.

It has been revealed that he brought a lot of Tesla’s power electronics talent with him. As we reported when Tesla first unveiled its transformer plans, Heron hired engineers who led power electronics design for Powerwall 3, the next-gen Megapack, and Superchargers, along with the person who ran Tesla’s power electronics controls team for charging and energy products.

Since then, Heron has raised a $38 million Series A, a $140 million Series B led by Andreessen Horowitz and Breakthrough Energy Ventures, and a $60 million credit facility from J.P. Morgan and TriplePoint Capital. Former Tesla CFO Zach Kirkhorn sits on its board, and Tesla co-founder JB Straubel is an investor.

Sources indicate that it’s also building Heron Factory One, a 286,000-square-foot plant in Morgan Hill, California, designed to make 10,000 Heron Links a year. That’s over 40 GW of annual capacity, with commercial production planned for late 2027.

Industry observers note that and the customers are lining up. Vantage reserved more than 1 GW for its data centers, Intersect reserved 1.5 GW, LG Energy Solution Vertech is integrating Heron Link with its US-made battery systems, and RWE signed a pilot to install Heron Links at a Texas battery storage site in April 2027. Baglino says Heron has 50 GW of orders in the pipeline.

Here’s how the two compare based on what each manufacturer has disclosed:.

In a recent development, on paper, Powercore is the bigger box, and now it has the better numbers too. At 7.4 MW continuous, it carries about 50% more power per unit than the 5 MW Heron Link, and its 98.86% peak efficiency edges out Heron’s 98.6%. But Tesla’s figure is a peak number, and Heron doesn’t label its own as one, so it’s not quite apples to apples. Neither company has shared pricing.

In a recent development, tesla is also going straight at Heron’s data center pitch. Powercore converts medium voltage directly to 800 Vdc, the rack architecture Nvidia is pushing, and Tesla indicates it’s working with Nvidia on 800 Vdc designs. Heron’s data center version does the same 34.5 kV AC to 800 VDC conversion with built-in storage, and data centers make up about a third of its business. Tesla’s answer to the storage piece is Megapack on the DC bus, and it says it already has 10 GWh of Megapack running at data centers.

This one is a little awkward for Tesla.

A major chunk of the people who designed Tesla’s power electronics over the last decade now work at Heron, and the guy who ran the whole org is its CEO. Tesla’s energy business also lost its longtime leader, Mike Snyder, last month, according to the WSJ.

This is all wrong. Tesla started developing this 3 years ago. Before Heron. The team selling Powercore is same as Megapack that has a way larger customer base than Heron. Also Heron is not a bankable organization per project finance terms. So they will struggle to get projects financed through equity and senior debt . Not as Tesla.

Industry observers note that to be fair, Tesla still has plenty of power electronics expertise. Its silicon carbide inverters are in millions of cars and every Megapack. And it has something Heron doesn’t: a massive installed base and a sales channel. Tesla says it’s almost sold out of Megapacks for 2027, and bundling Powercore into Megablock is an easy upsell. Plenty of developers will take the one-stop shop.

Tesla’s specs now match or beat Heron’s on paper. But Heron has named customers, a pilot site with an install date, and a factory under construction. Tesla has none of those yet. I wouldn’t be surprised if Heron is actually ahead here.

But either way, the transformer shortage is big enough for both companies to sell everything they can build.

As data centers and new solar and battery projects pile onto the grid, utilities are scrambling for equipment and passing those costs on to ratepayers. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Sources indicate that IF YOU WANT to gain muscle, your first instinct may be to head to the gym and hit the dumbbells. And while lifting will never go out of style (in our humble opinion), we're here to tell you that's not the only way to build strength. If you're short on gear—or even just want to shake things up—it's time to add some of the best resistance bands to your training arsenal.

Sources indicate that resistance bands are relatively affordable, lightweight, and compact. Most importantly, they're one of the most versatile strength accessories you can buy. Adding a resistance band into your routine can be as simple as integrating it into your bodyweight warmup, or looping it onto a kettlebell to add a little extra heat to a set of swings.

"Because of the elastic properties, resistance bands recruit muscle fibers differently than free weights," explains Juan Guadarrama, CSCS, one of the creators of Men’s Health’s "7-Minute Workouts for Fat Burn".

Of course, there are tons of different types of resistance bands (and resistance band exercises) out there, from closed loop bands, thick latex bands, and bands with handles to ones that use anchors to attach to your door. Depending on the thickness, they also provide different levels of resistance, meaning that not every band workout is for light weights.

Sources indicate that we've spent years testing dozens of the best exercise bands of nearly every type and thickness. Men's Health fitness editors, in collaboration with Men's Health Strength in Diversity initiative members Guadarrama and Eric Sung, CSCS (a trainer at Performance Lab in Fresh York City) have compared testing notes on the best resistance bands we've tried to break down what factors set the best apart from the rest.

It has been revealed that REP Fitness’s looped bands are durable, affordable, and have a wide weight range. With resistance profiles starting as low as five pounds (3X-Light) and as high as 150 (X-Heavy), users can gradually progress any exercise over time. They’re built with layered elastic and smoothed edges to create a smoother feel as the bands stretch and to reduce the chance of fraying (which can lead to breakage). The bands are color-coded and have the weight ranges printed clearly on each band, so I instantly know what I’m grabbing.

Marketed primarily as pull-up bands, their 38-inch length makes sense for assisted bodyweight work. However, for other moves—like curls or RDLs—that length can feel unwieldy. Still, with small adjustments, such as gripping lower on the band, double-looping the band, or widening your stance to take up slack, they function just great across a wide range of exercises.

The best value comes from REP’s five-band set (2X-Light through Heavy) at $70; it’s $50 cheaper than buying each band individually. Each band includes a one-year home-use warranty (and six months for commercial use).

Read More: The Best Items For Your Gym Bag.

Leekey’s bands cover most bases for most folks. If you’re looking for a middle-of-the-road set of looped bands to pack in your bag for travel workouts or to help with assisted pull-ups, dips, and push-ups, this is a solid choice for under $40. The brand offers many options, so carefully review the choices before selecting. With multiple bundle options available, I think the best value is one of the five-band sets with the included door anchor.

Because Leekey isn’t completely transparent about the build quality, proceed with caution before pulling these toward your face or looping them over barbells for heavy pulls. A small percentage of reviewers reported snapping, though it’s unclear whether they overstretched the bands. Still, the product holds a 4.6-star average across more than 11,500 reviews. One customer even posted a photo of the purple bands draped over a barbell loaded with 405 pounds, writing: “I have been using these bands for added resistance on deadlifts and rack pulls. They are holding up well and help with adding resistance at the lockout of the pull.”.

Read More: The Best Resistance Band Workouts.

Industry observers note that this set earns a spot for the sheer amount of resistance it offers—up to 300 pounds, more than any other kit on our list. That’s more than enough tension to challenge even advanced lifters. HPYGN also sells lighter-weight bundles at lower prices, but every option comes with the basics: a travel pouch, door anchor, handles, and ankle/wrist straps.

With over 10,000 reviews and a 4.5-star average, it’s an Amazon favorite. Some users note that bands have snapped under strain or that the listed resistance feels exaggerated, though the latter is subjective. On the flip side, many reviewers praise the sturdier build. One wrote: “I was pleasantly surprised that the gear looked like the ads and worked well. I bought it because of the metal carabiners that make it easy to change bands, and I wasn’t disappointed.”.

You’ll need a solid anchor point to get the most out of these, and long-term durability is a question mark. Still, if you’re trying to ditch your gym membership or want a heavy-duty band system for travel, HPYGN’s kit is a worthy pick. It’s affordable, versatile, and capable of potentially replacing machines and free weights.

Recent findings suggest that this rig gives you a little more than just the bands. We put this setup to the test, and found it to be super fun and intuitive to use. You can think of the Gorilla Bow as a hybrid tool that combines the benefits of resistance bands with a bow-style bar, which allows for a lot more versatility than a resistance band alone.

The unique bow design accommodates up to 300 pounds of resistance (just to start, you can get heavier models) that you can use to target just about every muscle group. The bow itself is made out of aircraft aluminum while the resistance bands are double-wall latex, resulting in a durable, lightweight, and portable build.

According to recent reports, resistance is adjustable, with the bow supporting up to four bands at a time so you can customize your resistance to meet your needs. The set comes with one original 56-inch bow, four Gorilla Bands (10, 20, 30 and 50-pounds), a band wrap, and a 30-day all-access membership to Gorilla Bow's virtual training platform. It's pricey, yes. But it packs a lot more usability than your average standalone resistance band.

Mini bands are a staple for warm-ups and recovery work, often wrapped around the knees for lateral walks or used to cue better glute and abductor activation during squats. Titan’s version is a little different. Designed initially as attachments for the brand’s Vice Grip Trainer, these bands double as standalone mini bands. And because they’re built for machine resistance, they’re thicker, more durable, and provide far greater tension than typical minis.

The resistance ranges from 15 pounds up to 120 pounds, which means the lightest bands are great for activation drills, while the heavy green band can push your lateral walks well past warm-up territory.

Recent findings suggest that the catch is price. At nearly $50, these cost significantly more than most mini-band sets, and their uses are inherently limited compared to looped or tube bands. Still, the build quality is excellent, and the extra resistance opens the door for more challenging work than you’ll get with cheaper, flimsier bands. If you’re willing to invest once for a set that won’t wear out quickly, Titan’s mini bands are a “buy once, cry once” purchase.

It has been revealed that rogue is synonymous with quality in the fitness equipment space, and its tube resistance bands live up to the reputation. If you’re looking for bands to actually build workouts around—not just warm up with—these are among the best. The textured rubber handles stand out: they’re coated in a knurl-like pattern that gives you a secure grip, even when your hands get sweaty.

In a recent development, I noted that REP Fitness’s loop bands were long at 38 inches, and Rogue’s bands clock even longer at an elastic length of 48 inches. However, the length does allow you to perform overhead presses, lateral raises, and kickbacks with the bands. To increase the tension, loop the band around a squat rack or pole and take a few steps back. (Though Rogue warns customers not to overstretch the band.) Each band is a standalone product, so you can’t clip multiple elastic tubes to a pair of handles, as with other models.

In a recent development, price-wise, individual bands cost a bit more than some competitors, but Rogue makes up for it with bundle pricing. A light set (bands 0-2) runs $36.50, the heavy set (3-5) is $45, and the full collection is $75. Considering the quality and the savings versus buying separately, the sets are where the real value lies. For those who want tube bands tough enough for serious training, Rogue delivers.

It has been revealed that these resistance bands feature four tubes braided together to create a durable workout tool that can stand up to your toughest sessions. We love that users can choose from five resistance levels, ranging from feather-light to heavy-duty, and select the perfect size and tension based on their preferences and fitness level. We found the handles comfortable, featuring a protective sleeve and grommet reinforcement which helps to ensure a solid grip.

In a recent development, while they excel in mobility work, don't expect crazy heavy resistance. They come in five resistance levels, from 'very light' to 'very heavy', ranging from 3 to 27 pounds. The various levels also differ in length, ranging from the 44-inch very light cord to the very heavy 53-inch cord, so you can pick the size and tension right for you.

If you want to go all in with resistance bands, WHATAFIT offers five bands (10, 20, 30, 40, 50-pound listed resistances), handles, ankle straps, a door anchor, and a carrying pouch. Some bundles even come with additional looped or mini bands. You’re not going to get much closer to having a complete gym in your home—especially for under $40—than with this set.

Sources indicate that the set is also wildly popular: With a 4.6-star average and over 34,000 reviews—more than any other band on this list—it has the people’s approval. You can stack the bands for more precise resistance, which makes progressive overload easier and mimics the flexibility you’d get in a commercial gym. As one reviewer put it: “The materials feel high-quality and durable, and the bands have held up really well so far. I’ve used them for upper body, lower body, and core training without any problems. Plus, the whole set is compact and easy to store or travel with.”.

In a recent development, what holds it back slightly is that these bands are serviceable, not premium. While natural latex is great for elasticity, it can degrade over time with sweat, sun, and repeated stretch cycles, so expect some wear. That stated, for the price, this set offers a wide breadth of use and works well for someone building up strength or who needs a versatile “one-stop” band kit.

Your most important consideration should be how you initiative to use your resistance bands—for solo workouts, to add resistance to exercises, to help you with dips or pull-ups, or to warm up before your lifts. No one band will perfectly check every box.

Most resistance bands are made from latex and rubber (or some combination of the two) and use plastic parts for accessories like handles and door anchors. (If you have a latex allergy, there are latex-free resistance bands.) So we’re not going to list materials as a significant consideration.

Industry observers note that likewise, the bands in this guide are all similar in price, with no major outliers. Premium and/or unique band designs cost more, but expect to pay between $20 and $70 for bands. The price scales based on the band resistance and whether or not you’re buying a set. Below are the top three things you should consider when shopping around for a upcoming resistance band.

It has been revealed that the type of band you buy dictates the kind of workouts you can perform. Here’s a quick breakdown of the band styles you’ll see, save for a few unique models, most of which are on this list.

Sources indicate that also referred to as super bands, these are the quintessential resistance bands that most manufacturers sell. Because the band is a single loop, you have to get creative in performing specific exercises, but you can target most major muscles with a looped band. You can also wrap them around pull-up bars, barbells, and machines to change the resistance profile of an exercise.

According to recent reports, popular in physical therapy offices, mini bands are an excellent tool for activating the smaller muscles in your hips, legs, upper back, and shoulders. They can’t support your bodyweight and they don’t stretch far enough to allow for squats, presses, or curls. Think of these as a warm-up tool, not a workout replacement.

According to recent reports, these bands are defined by a single tube of rubber with a handle on each end (usually). These bands give you the most freedom of movement, and the handles allow you to press and row more efficiently (compared to looped bands).

Sources indicate that some bands cite a single poundage versus a range. If a band lists its resistance as between 20 and 60 force, you’ll experience 20 pounds of resistance when the band is least stretched and 60 pounds at the most stretched position. Squatting with a 50-pound band doesn’t feel the same as squatting with a 50-pound dumbbell, either, since the force you’re resisting is literally changing with every inch you move.

Recent findings suggest that to track your progress effectively, find a band that has you reaching within one to three reps of failure for your desired rep range. Stick with that band until the reps feel easier, and then move up to the next heaviest band you have. Progressing with bands isn’t as easy as with free weights and machines, but you'll make gains as long as you’re basing your effort on training intensity and not weight.

It has been revealed that resistance bands can be dangerous. If they snap while doing assisted pull-ups or a face pull, you’ll fall or injure your eyes or face. No band is wear-proof, so it’s essential to use them responsibly: don’t overstretch, inspect them regularly for tears, and avoid anchoring them against textured surfaces like the knurling on a barbell, which creates friction that weakens the material.

Manufacturers use different strategies to improve longevity. Some bands are built from layered latex for added reinforcement, while others encase the elastic in a protective sleeve that reduces wear and shields the user from a whip-like snap mid-rep. These features can’t eliminate risk, but they can extend the lifespan of your bands and make training safer.

Recent findings suggest that as a longtime fitness journalist and NASM-certified trainer, I have spent years using resistance bands in a variety of exercise scenarios. For this story, I worked in tandem with the team at Men's Health, including Fitness Director Ebenezer Samuel, CSCS, and Fitness and Commerce Editor Charles Thorp, NASM. We also recruited the help of MH Strength in Diversity members Juan Guadarrama, CSCS and Eric Sung, CSCS to gather diverse perspectives on the topic.

We used our collective experience to put together a testing pool by putting the most popular designs that we could put up against newly introduced offerings from classic brands as well as newcomers to the market. Both historically and in the pursuit of this story, we used these designs during band-only workouts, athletic movements, and to advance fundamental movements like the deadlift. The selections above represent the best resistance bands that you can buy now.

We asked Strength in Diversity member Eric Sung about his favorite ways to incorporate resistance bands with clients and in his own training.

Sources indicate that "The banded rear delt fly is great exercise to do as a warm up to prepare your body before an upper body session," says Sung. "Grab the band, hold it out in front of you, stretch it across your upper chest and try to resist the band as much and slowly as you can.".

In a recent development, if you're looking to get started in training lower body plyometrics, put band-assisted squat jumps on your radar. "Tie a band to a high anchor, grab each end of it, assume your squat stance, and focus on jumping as high as you can with the assistance of the band. This is a great entry point," he adds.

For more ideas, check out our list of 12 resistance band workouts you can do at home.

Industry observers note that similar to free weights, resistance bands help create tension and place stress on the muscles, explains Sung. However, resistance bands assist in efforts to build muscle and strength in a few unique ways.

Industry observers note that because they deliver more resistance as you stretch them further, they offer a different challenge than free weights. This means your muscles face the most load and tension at the top of every exercise. For example, the top of a resistance band pushup is a challenge; the top of a bodyweight pushup is a position of rest.

It has been revealed that another way resistance bands help build strength is by assisting in movements that an individual cannot yet complete at baseline standards, explains Guadarrama. "It allows athletes to move through the full range of motion and acquire neuromuscular capacity," he explains. "Over time the body can adapt, learn the movement, and build the strength needed for the unassisted effort.".

Bands can also be attached to plates and kettlebells to add more resistance to the eccentric or concentric phases of a given movement, explains Guadarrama. "Each of these methods has benefits to biomechanical advantages and providing variance in stress," he says.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A nuclear submarine recently returned to Scotland after setting a Royal Navy record of 217 days underwater. The HMS Vengeance’s seven-month deployment overtook the 205-day milestone set by the HMS Vanguard in April. But with the Vengeance crew finally back home, critics now argue the two submarines’ lengthy back-to-back voyages are causes for concern, not celebration.

“The fleet was designed around three-month tours, and that was considered to be a long time to be stuck underwater in a metal box with no contact with the outside world,” nuclear submarine expert David Cullen told The Guardian on November 15.

The 17,526-ton, nearly 500-foot-long HMS Vengeance is one of Britain’s four Vanguard-class submarines constructed to carry monstrous Trident nuclear missiles. First introduced in 1998, the vessel features 16 missile tubes, each loaded with one Trident containing up to a dozen, 100-kiloton multiple independently targetable reentry vehicles (MIRVs). The MIRV is specifically engineered to simultaneously deploy a payload of individual nuclear weapons aimed at a list of targets. The Royal Navy continuously keeps at least one Vanguard submarine at sea, which hypothetically allows the United Kingdom to still conduct nuclear strikes in the event its land-based systems are compromised during a nuclear war.

According to recent reports, vanguard submarines were originally built to host around 140 crewmembers during three-to-four month deployments. Although a 100-day excursion was once considered rare, underwater stints are now often double the length of time, forcing sailors to stack extra provisions along already cramped corridors and inside any additional nooks. The U.K. government attributes the extended missions to budgetary cuts that have dramatically slowed down the pace of multimillion-dollar vessel maintenance projects.

According to recent reports, deployment aboard a submarine like the Vengeance is considered one of the navy’s most psychologically difficult assignments. The nuclear sub remains underwater in total radio silence for the entire length of a patrol to keep its position secret. The vessel can travel to a depth of around 984 feet, but it may occasionally ascend to shallower waters to communicate via a transmission buoy or floating wire antenna. Crewmembers may receive a weekly, 120-word “Familygram” message, but each dispatch is previewed by naval officials. These readers retain the right to censor any bad news or information they feel may compromise sailors’ effectiveness. Regardless of what a sailor ultimately reads, they are strictly prohibited from responding.

In a recent development, the toll on crew is steep, but it’s particularly difficult for the women comprising roughly 10-percent of the navy. In 2022, whistleblower Sophie Brook generated international headlines after reporting a “constant campaign of sexual bullying” while serving as one of the Royal Navy’s first female submariners. In 2024, First Sea Lord Adm. Sir Ben Key called the crew misogyny “intolerable” and apologized to the growing number of women who subsequently came forward with their own stories. The Royal Navy’s investigations ultimately resulted in the firing, demotion, and disciplining of dozens of servicemen—including Key’s own termination.

Recent findings suggest that key’s successor, Gen. Sir Gwyn Jenkins, stated he had “nothing but tremendous respect” for Trident crews earlier this month, while admitting the need to “improve our submarine maintenance.”.

The Vanguard fleet was designed for about 25 years of service, but will likely accumulate roughly four decades of sailing by the time its first replacement is ready. That submarine, the HMS Dreadnought, isn’t expected to sail until around 2032.

Taking Fish Oil to Boost Brain Health? A 2-Year Study Questions the Benefits

📅 29 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1046 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A clinical trial found that taking high dose omega-3 supplements for 2 years did not help memory or thinking skills in older adults at increased risk of Alzheimer’s.Researchers at Keck Medicine of USC led the study, which was published in eBioMedicine.
  • Getting omega-3s from food or supplements is key since the body cannot make them.
  • Keck Medicine researchers enrolled 365 adults who did not have dementia, and whose ages ranged from 55 to 80, with an average age of 66.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A clinical trial found that taking high dose omega-3 supplements for 2 years did not help memory or thinking skills in older adults at increased risk of Alzheimer’s.Researchers at Keck Medicine of USC led the study, which was published in eBioMedicine. Participants took either a daily high dose supplement of omega-3 fatty acid docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) or a placebo.Fish oil is one of the most familiar ways people get omega-3s. However, the supplement in this clinical trial wasn’t made from fish, Hussein Yassine, MD, director of the USC Center for Personalized Brain Health with Keck Medicine of USC and the study’s lead researcher, told Healthline. This article uses the broader term omega-3 supplements.The researchers found that taking supplements raised omega-3 levels in participants’ brains, yet it didn’t change their memory, thinking skills, or brain structure.Dung Trinh, MD, an internist at MemorialCare Medical Group and chief medical officer of Healthy Brain Clinic in Irvine, California, who wasn’t involved in the study, told Healthline that the findings challenge the common belief that omega-3 supplements, such as fish oil, can help prevent Alzheimer’s disease or improve memory.Millions of older adults take omega-3 supplements. In a 2017–2018 federal survey, 21.8% of U.S. adults age 60 and older reported taking an omega-3 fatty acid supplement in the past 30 days, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

Getting omega-3s from food or supplements is key since the body cannot make them.

Keck Medicine researchers enrolled 365 adults who did not have dementia, and whose ages ranged from 55 to 80, with an average age of 66.

Subjects obtained little DHA from their diets and had at least one risk factor for dementia. Of the 365 people who enrolled, 225 completed the trial, according to the study. Nearly half (47%) carried APOE4.Participants took either 2,000 milligrams (mg) of DHA or a placebo every day. Neither participants nor researchers knew who received the supplement.

The supplement in the trial contained more than 90% DHA and about 1% EPA, Yassine remarked.

Researchers found that high dose omega-3 supplements raised DHA levels in the fluid around the brain and spinal cord by 17%.

Industry observers note that both groups in the trial scored about the same on memory and thinking tests. Brain structure appeared the same in both groups.

Sources indicate that the supplement also raised omega-3 levels in the blood. Over two years, participants’ omega-3 index, a measure of EPA and DHA in red blood cells, rose from 4.9% to 11%.“That’s a massive increase, but that doesn’t translate into clinical outcomes,” Yassine said.DHA reached the brain equally well in people with and without the gene variant APOE4, which is linked to a higher risk of Alzheimer’s disease, according to the study.Earlier trials couldn’t tell whether DHA failed to reach the brain or reached it without helping, the study’s authors say. This trial answers that open question, since the DHA got there.“This tells us that just because a supplement reaches the brain doesn’t necessarily mean it will improve brain function or prevent cognitive decline,” Trinh said.

The lack of measurable change in memory and thinking may come down to how the body uses omega-3s, according to Yassine.He said it’s “really important to distinguish between omega-3 metabolism and omega-3 supplements.”A supplement can raise omega-3 levels, yet the body may still break them down before they reach the right places. Obesity, smoking, and a lack of exercise can all reduce how much omega-3 gets into the brain, he said.

Some fish and fish oil supplements may offer more than omega-3s. These sources may also include other nutrients such as lutein, vitamin E, and selenium, Yassine said.A supplement can raise the level, but if you don’t change the holistic program, just going and increasing the level by itself may not be sufficient,” he said.Researchers tend to fall into two camps on how to read the results, according to Yassine.

According to recent reports, some see the findings as evidence that supplements don’t work in isolation. Others argue the trial would need a longer follow-up or sicker participants to answer the question.Trinh pointed to the study’s length. “It’s also notable to recognize that Alzheimer’s disease develops over decades, so a two-year study may not be long enough to determine whether DHA supplementation has any long-term preventive benefits,” he mentioned.

Fish oil supplements contain two omega-3 fatty acids, eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and DHA, according to the National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NCCIH).

Foods such as fish and flaxseed also contain omega-3s, according to the National Institutes of Health’s Office of Dietary Supplements (ODS).Research suggests omega-3s may help reduce inflammation, support heart health, and promote childhood growth and development.

Some observational studies link diets high in omega-3s with a lower risk of cognitive decline and dementia.

Recent findings suggest that researchers say omega-3s may help preserve cognition by supporting brain cells in continuing to function and maintain their membranes, according to the ODS.“Omega-3s are notable for the brain, and we and many others have shown that having higher levels of omega-3s is associated with less Alzheimer’s pathology, better cognition, and many other protective outcomes,” Yassine noted, in contrast to the trial findings.Trinh agreed. “DHA plays an essential role in maintaining healthy brain cells, and there is evidence that eating fish as part of a healthy dietary pattern may support long-term brain health,” he said.Research on omega-3s and brain health is ongoing, and there is insufficient evidence to draw firm conclusions about their effectiveness.

Some people may still benefit from a supplement, according to Yassine, including:.

Some neurologists test omega-3 levels, though the test isn’t standard, Yassine stated.People with nutritional deficiencies or certain genetic or metabolic traits may respond differently to omega-3 supplements, and researchers still need to learn who might benefit, Trinh said.

People who already take fish oil or other omega-3 supplements for other reasons, such as high triglycerides, should make those decisions with their healthcare professionals, he stated.

Trinh stated he tells his patients that “what is good for the heart is generally good for the brain.” He recommended the following healthy habits:.

“Overall, this study reminds us that there is no magic pill for preventing Alzheimer’s disease and that maintaining brain health requires a much broader approach,” Trinh mentioned.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The iX5 is BMW’s first fully electric vehicle built in the US, promising an estimated up to 456 miles of range, ultra-fast charging speeds, and plenty of Neue Klasse tech.
  • BMW officially opened its new Plant Woodruff in South Carolina on November 13, marking the start of series production of its sixth-generation (Gen6) electric vehicle batteries.
  • The Gen6 batteries will power BMW’s upcoming “X” electric vehicles, starting with the all-new iX5 SUV.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The iX5 is BMW’s first fully electric vehicle built in the US, promising an estimated up to 456 miles of range, ultra-fast charging speeds, and plenty of Neue Klasse tech.

BMW officially opened its new Plant Woodruff in South Carolina on November 13, marking the start of series production of its sixth-generation (Gen6) electric vehicle batteries.

The Gen6 batteries will power BMW’s upcoming “X” electric vehicles, starting with the all-new iX5 SUV.

The iX5 is being built about 15 miles away at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg, the firm’s first fully electric model to be assembled in the US.

BMW Plant Spartanburg is churning out around 70 iX5s a day following a $1.7 billion investment in South Carolina to expand the plant for EV production and build the upcoming battery assembly plant in Woodruff.

According to Robert Engelhorn, president and CEO of BMW Manufacturing in Spartanburg, the company is confident the iX5 will attract buyers, promising 435 miles of range, ultra-fast charging, and its updated Neue Klasse technology and design.

Engelhorn told Automotive News in an interview that “there’s a clear trend globally for EVs,” adding that “We will contribute to this growth from the BMW side.”.

BMW didn’t provide a specific production estimate for the iX5, but suppliers were reportedly told it would be around 60,000 EVs in 2027, down from 100,000 it initially forecasted.

“We said we would begin assembling fully electric BMW vehicles in the US by the end of 2026 – and we are delivering on that commitment,” Engelhorn said.

A company spokesperson confirmed that the iX5 will initially use battery cells from China before switching to US-sourced cells from LG Energy Solutions plant in Arizona by the end of the decade.

With production now underway, the iX5 is expected to begin arriving at US dealerships in early 2027.

It has been revealed that the 2027 BMW iX5 60 xDrive starts at $79,800. BMW estimates the 144 kWh battery will provide up to 456 miles of range, up from the 435 miles it previously estimated.

Sources indicate that it features BMW’s fresh “double-X” light signature, which combines the headlights, daytime running lights, side lights, and turn signals into one unit. The Double-X headlights come standard, but BMW said you can switch them for simpler diagonal stripes.

Last month, BMW showcased the i5’s ultra-fast-charging capabilities during a media event in Southern California with IONNA and Alpitronic.

During the demo, the iX5 60 xDrive hit a peak of 464 kW, which BMW mentioned enables it to add an impressive up to 170 miles of range in 10 minutes.

Industry observers note that the electric SUV features a dual-motor all-wheel-drive powertrain setup that delivers a combined 578 hp (425 kW) and 593 lb-ft of torque. BMW claims it can go from 0 to 60 mph in 4.4 seconds and tow up to 6,000 lbs.

Inside, the iX5 adopts BMW’s Neue Klasse design and tech, like the smaller iX3 SUV. The setup includes a upcoming 17.9″ infotainment touchscreen and BMW’s Panoramic Vision, which spans the bottom of the windshield. There’s also an optional 14.6″ passenger screen for a third display.

This is at the top of our short list. Out of Spec got 411 miles at 70 mph (by contrast the Gravity rated at 450 got 368 on the same run and the R1S rated at 410 got 349). It is a real 400+ mile vehicle with an ability to charge a real 300 miles in ~20 minutes.

According to recent reports, edit: OOS was with 22" wheels rated at 426. It should get >430 with the standard 21" wheels.

Measuring 197.2″ long, 78.7″ wide, and 68.9″ tall, BMW’s new iX5 is about the size of the Porsche Cayenne Electric.

By 2030, BMW intends to be assembling at least fully electric models at Plant Spartanburg. “This marks the beginning of the next chapter in the success story of the largest plant in our global production network,” Raymond Wittman, BMW’s head of production, said.

Following Debrecen (Hungary), Irlbach-Straßkirchen (Germany), and Shenyang (China), Woodruff is the fourth site in BMW’s production network to begin series production of the Gen6 batteries.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that when you're short on space (or even if you're not), having an extra set of drawers on hand is a huge boon for small bedrooms. That's where the best storage beds come in. I'm all about bedroom furniture that does more for your sleep setup, so I gathered up a few favorites from the AD staff. These storage bed picks include sleek, streamlined designs with completely concealed side storage, queen- and king-size beds with pullouts at the footboard, and more. Each one stows generously while you sleep.

Sources indicate that A storage bed frame need not be ugly, even if function is the whole point of buying one. In fact, I tapped other editors and we found impressive wooden beds from Thuma and West Elm, the upholstered storage beds of our minimalist dreams from Saatva, Article, and Sundays, and a lilac velvet showpiece from CB2 for anyone who wants their storage bed to be the loudest thing in the room. The market has our back on this one, especially for those of us living in shoebox bedrooms where a queen bed barely fits, let alone a nightstand (the luxury). Below are the 10 storage beds I considered up to snuff, with editor commentary.

All prices in this article reflect queen-size beds unless otherwise noted.

All prices in this article reflect queen-size beds unless otherwise noted.

Bed frame reviewer: Kate McGregor, contributor.

What attracted you to this bed frame? Like any girl living in Fresh York in her mid-20s, I have a lot of stuff. And while I have ample closet space (a rarity), I like a certain level of type-A organization. Closed or hidden storage is key, and I didn’t want to fill my precious closet space with off-season sweaters and formalwear I reach for once a year. Enter: a platform storage bed. Not taking up any extra square footage was key, or else I would have bought a trunk or bookcase like my mother suggested. I had several coworkers who swore by Saatva’s mattresses for both quality and comfort, so investing in their furniture felt like a natural next step. The Halle bed frame is one of their more minimal silhouettes that I knew would suit my ever-evolving design style.

Sources indicate that what was the delivery and assembly like? Delivery and assembly were a breeze. The team gave me an hour's notice before arriving, so I could prep my space (aka move my Amazon bed frame out of the way and vacuum). Assembly took about an hour, and the three-man team was incredibly efficient. They checked in with me multiple times throughout the process to ensure they got the placement exactly right. Afterward, they left with all the trash and packaging in tow, and they even helped me place my 150-pound mattress back onto the new frame.

According to recent reports, are there any standout features? The lift mechanism is really much smoother than I'd expected. Durable linen handles ensure that I'm never fighting for grip on the base. If I'm really feeling it, I can lift the base with one hand to access the storage below.

According to recent reports, what’s your bedroom design, and how does this storage bed align with your aesthetic? My bedroom is quite minimal—jute rug, dark wood dresser, cream linen curtains. I change my bedding at every whim, so I wanted a bed frame that wouldn't take up too much attention from my gingham sheets and block-printed quilt. The beige linen frame does just that, it serves as a neutral backdrop for whatever bedding layers I choose.

Industry observers note that did the bed frame live up to your expectations? Yes, and then some. Over the last eight months, this bed has remained sturdy, and without being too dramatic, it has revolutionized my apartment’s storage. Christmas garlands, high heels, and even craft supplies have all found a home in the spacious cavity. Plus, the raised base keeps all of my belongings off the ground. The linen fabric has softened a bit with age, especially on the headboard and handles that I’m touching more frequently than the frame. The lift mechanisms are easy to use and lock while lifted, allowing me to maneuver in the storage space without holding the bed up. The lift even handles my 150-pound mattress with ease, not even creasing a pillow.

How would you rate the sturdiness of this bed frame on a scale of 1–10? The sturdiness is a 9/10—I dock it a point only because I pushed my bed frame and it shifted a bit away from the storage base. Otherwise, there's no movement, creaking, or stability complications, even as I toss and turn.

Would you recommend this bed frame to a friend? Absolutely. This bed is a major investment, I won’t lie. But I don’t blueprint on needing a different bed frame anytime soon (maybe ever), so the longevity of this bed is well worth the price point.

Bed frame reviewer: Zoë Sessums, contributor.

What attracted you to this bed frame? I have a small house and I am constantly rearranging rooms, so I was drawn to the easy assembly and disassembly potential of the Thuma bed. I wanted to be able to set up the frame, take it apart, move it around, and do that repeatedly. Plus, I like how clean the lines are and how versatile the style is. With the drawer component, I loved that I can easily move these around too. They are perfect for storing extra bedding like sheets, pillows, and duvets.

According to recent reports, what was the delivery and assembly like? Everything came in a manageable sized box so I could unpack and assemble the bed and drawers quickly and without stress. The drawers simply needed to be unboxed and placed under the frame. Truthfully, I think the hardest part is breaking down the cardboard.

According to recent reports, are there any standout features? I think the fact that the bed requires no tools for assembly is a pro for most. No need to keep track of your Allen keys or dread a move. The fact that you can now add integrated underbed storage is even better. The drawers have wheels so they slide seamlessly on the floor and the whole process is easy and enjoyable.

What’s your bedroom design, and how does this storage bed align with your aesthetic? My bedroom design is minimalist. I like to have little distractions and clutter in the sleeping sanctuary—I try to channel sleek, Scandinavian sensibilities. The storage is great for keeping things organized and out of sight. I like how the simple design blends right in with the bed frame.

Did the bed frame live up to your expectations? Please describe your sleep experience with this bed frame. I’ve had my Thuma frame for years now and it’s held up wonderfully with moves, room changes, and many restful nights. The frame provides great structure and comfort. The drawers are a fresh added bonus. I predict they will hold up as well as the frame.

How would you rate the sturdiness of this bed frame on a scale of 1–10? An 8.5.

Sources indicate that would you recommend this bed frame to a friend? Ten thousand percent. This bed frame will hold up and you can add several drawers for added storage.

Bed frame reviewer: Lisa Aiken, senior vice president of shopping at Condé Nast.

Industry observers note that what attracted you to this bed frame? The statement made by the large wingback cushioned headboard really made this bed frame stand out, giving a less usual silhouette and making a visual impact in the space of the primary bedroom. I am always on the lookout for extra storage, and the three large built-in drawers are exactly what I needed.

What was the delivery and assembly like? Delivery and assembly were white glove and handled by a third party. It was a mixed experience. The customer service and booking experience was excellent, helpful and well informed, providing a clear date and delivery window of my choosing and easily changing the date without any issues when I needed to amend. The actual delivery and assembly were less impressive, missing the five-hour delivery window by 90 minutes and then taking two movers almost two hours to assemble the bed frame, which I believe is more to do with the complex construction of the frame than anything else. That stated, the movers were very polite and respectful and removed all of the excess packing.

Are there any standout features? There are two standout features: Aesthetically, the wingback headboard is very eye-catching, providing a visually interesting form. Practically, the storage that this bed frame provides is substantial, especially the large full-width drawer at the foot of the bed.

It has been revealed that what’s your bedroom design, and how does this storage bed align with your aesthetic? The bedroom is a large mid-century modern and minimalist space with lots of natural light and requires large pieces of furniture to match the scale of the room, which this bed frame provides. The subtle color shade of the fabric and the wingback design of the headboard fit perfectly with the natural light and the high ceilings to make a relaxing and inviting bedroom.

Did the bed frame live up to your expectations? The fully upholstered and cushioned frame with its neutral fabric creates a very cozy and relaxing sleeping environment, the scale of the headboard provides the statement that I had hoped for, and the overall quality of the bed is high. The three storage drawers are very spacious and easy to access, providing me with a significant amount of extra storage.

Sources indicate that how would you rate the sturdiness of this bed frame on a scale of 1-10? Eight out of 10. The frame is very sturdy. The slats are thick wood, providing a very stable and solid base for the mattress and brace for the bed frame, which both increases the comfort level and provides a sturdy structure with very little movement—something that has previously been an problem with other king bed frames I have owned. There is a slight misalignment of the drawers, not noticeable with a mattress and bedding.

Would you recommend this bed frame to a friend? Yes, I would recommend this frame with a few reservations. It is very functional; providing a large amount of storage, it is a comfortable and sturdy bed frame. The fabric is of good quality matching the colorway shown online with the look of linen despite being predominantly durable polyester. The reservations would be the assembly time, which is significantly longer than other bed frames I have had, and a slight misalignment of the side drawers—which is not noticeable once the bed is made.

Overall, it represents good value for money given size, comfort, and the aesthetic it provides.

Industry observers note that editor's note: The Article Cigar bed frame Aiken originally tested is no longer in stock. The Kayra upholstered storage bed has a similar fully upholstered look, though its storage comes as four side drawers rather than the Cigar's single drawer at the foot of the bed.

Bed frame reviewer: Lisa Aiken, senior vice president of shopping at Condé Nast.
